content: Illness, sometimes referred to as ill-health, is defined as a state of poor health. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), health is described as a state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity (WHO, 1946). When these conditions are not met, an individual can be considered to have an illness or to be ill. Pharmacology and medication are utilized to treat or alleviate the symptoms of illnesses or medical conditions. Developmental disability refers to severe, lifelong disabilities caused by mental and/or physical impairments. Abnormal conditions of the body or mind that result in discomfort, dysfunction, or distress to the affected individual or those around them are classified as illnesses. The term illness is sometimes broadly applied to include injuries, disabilities, syndromes, infections, symptoms, deviant behaviors, and atypical variations in structure or function. In other contexts, these may be categorized separately. A pathogen or infectious agent is a biological entity that causes disease or illness in its host. A passenger virus, on the other hand, is a virus that resides in or infects the body without causing symptoms, illness, or disease. Foodborne illness, also known as food poisoning, occurs when food contaminated with pathogenic bacteria, toxins, viruses, prions, or parasites is consumed. Mental illness, also referred to as emotional disability or cognitive dysfunction, is a broad term encompassing a range of conditions characterized by emotional instability, behavioral dysregulation, and/or cognitive impairment. Examples of specific mental illnesses include major depression, generalized anxiety disorder, schizophrenia, and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Mental illnesses can arise from various causes, including trauma or conflict, and may impair an individual's ability to work, attend school, or maintain relationships. Other terms for mental illness include mental disorder, psychiatric disorder, psychological disorder, abnormal psychology, emotional disability, emotional problems, or behavior problems. The term insanity is used in a legal context. Brain damage can result from a variety of conditions, illnesses, or injuries. A delusion is defined as a fixed false belief. In everyday language, it refers to a belief that is false, fanciful, or derived from deception. In psychiatry, the term is more precise, indicating that the belief is pathological and results from an illness or disease process. Munchausen syndrome involves individuals feigning, exaggerating, or creating symptoms of illness in themselves to gain medical attention, treatment, or sympathy. Munchausen syndrome by proxy involves inducing illness in another person for similar reasons. A mental health consumer is an individual receiving treatment for a psychiatric illness or disorder. This term was introduced to empower individuals with mental health issues, emphasizing their role in choosing their treatment and highlighting their importance to the existence of mental health providers. Social determinants of health refer to the social conditions in which people live, which significantly influence their health. Illnesses are often linked to social, economic, political, and environmental factors. Organizations such as the Public Health Agency of Canada and the World Health Organization recognize the profound impact of social determinants on collective and individual well-being. Government involvement is crucial in studying various illnesses and treatments. Healthcare encompasses the prevention, treatment, and management of illness, as well as the preservation of mental and physical well-being, through services provided by medical, nursing, and allied health professionals. The organized provision of these services constitutes a healthcare system. Before the term healthcare became common, English speakers referred to medicine or the health sector and discussed the treatment and prevention of illness and disease. A patient is any individual receiving medical attention, care, or treatment, typically due to illness or injury. The term health consumer or healthcare consumer is often used interchangeably with patient by governmental agencies, insurance companies, and patient advocacy groups. Medical emergencies are injuries or illnesses that pose an immediate threat to a person's health or life, requiring urgent medical attention. Emergency medicine is a specialized field focusing on the effective management of medical emergencies and patient resuscitation. Emergency departments provide initial treatment for a wide range of illnesses and injuries, some of which may be life-threatening and require immediate care. A drug is any chemical substance, other than food or devices, that affects the function of living organisms. Drugs can be used to treat illnesses or recreationally to alter behavior and perception. Medications are typically produced by pharmaceutical companies and are often patented. Non-patented medications are referred to as generic drugs. Physicians may prescribe approved medications for uses other than their intended indications, a practice known as off-label use. Overdosing on a drug, where it is consumed in quantities or concentrations that overwhelm the body's homeostasis, can result in severe illness or death. This is essentially a form of poisoning. In biological terms, poisons are substances that can cause illness. Bed rest, as a medical treatment, involves remaining in bed continuously as a therapeutic measure, such as for recovery from a hangover. While hospitalized patients often spend much of their time in bed, bed rest typically refers to extended periods of recumbence at home. Human enhancement technologies (HET) are tools that can be used not only to treat illness and disability but also to enhance human capacities and characteristics. Medication is a licensed drug taken to cure or alleviate symptoms of an illness or medical condition. A wheelchair is a mobility device designed for individuals who cannot walk due to illness or disability. Shock therapy involves the deliberate induction of a physiological state of shock in an individual for psychiatric treatment purposes. Electrotherapy uses electrical energy to treat health impairments and conditions of abnormal functioning. Epidemiology is the scientific study of factors affecting the health and illness of individuals and populations. It serves as the foundation for public health interventions and preventive medicine. Behavioral medicine is an interdisciplinary field that integrates psychosocial, behavioral, and biomedical knowledge relevant to health and illness. The Clinical Global Impression scale is used to assess treatment response in patients with mental disorders. Its Improvement scale requires clinicians to evaluate how much a patient's illness has improved or worsened relative to a baseline state. Mental confusion and decreased alertness may indicate a worsening of a chronic illness.
